analysis_role: post-result descriptive audit asking whether unequal relative evolutionary depth can be reduced to simple differences in minimum-change burden

orientation_vs_phyllary.interpretation: similar coverage-adjusted minimum-change burden coexists with distinct depth placement

stickiness_vs_orientation.interpretation: stickiness is both somewhat more step-dense under the coverage normalization and substantially shallower

allowed_inference: Relative evolutionary-depth differences contain information not captured by simple minimum-step burden.
Orientation and phyllary have similar coverage-adjusted minimum-change burden but differ in relative-depth placement.
Stickiness is the shallow pole and also has a modestly higher coverage-adjusted minimum-change burden.
not_allowed: The three traits have equal evolutionary rates or equal lability.
Minimum steps per resolved concept is a rate per unit evolutionary time.
Cross-trait burden is fully commensurable despite different state ontologies, especially the four-state phyllary character.
Unequal depth proves module-specific selection or adaptation.
manuscript_consequence: Replace strong wording that modules differ in depth but not changeability with the bounded statement that depth stratification is not explained away by simple coverage-adjusted minimum-change burden; equal lability remains unestablished.
